messages.text:
"Create a high-end, photorealistic survival horror game titled \"The Facility: Null\". 
Take all the time required to generate, build, script, and polish every visual asset, UI element, voice line, and mechanic to absolute perfection, regardless of how long it takes.

0. CREATOR CREDIT @COMMENT_BODY@ TITLE SCREEN:
- Display the game title prominently on the main menu as: \"The Facility: Null\"
- Directly below the title, include the credit line: \"Created by °-° KING LOOK.S\" / \"Idee @COMMENT_BODY@ Konzept von °-° KING LOOK.S\" in a sleek, glowing metallic font.

1. LANGUAGE @COMMENT_BODY@ AUDIO SETTINGS:
- Language Options: The game settings, UI text, inventory, subtitles, and menus must be fully localized with a language switcher between German and English. 
- Menus @COMMENT_BODY@ Settings: Displayed in German by default (e.g., \"Einstellungen\", \"Grafik\", \"Multiplayer\", \"Steuerung\").
- Voice Acting @COMMENT_BODY@ Audio: All in-game dialogue, audio logs, radio calls, and character voices must remain in full, crystal-clear, professional English with precise 3D binaural spatial audio.

2. GRAPHICS @COMMENT_BODY@ VISUAL QUALITY:
- Photorealistic visual quality powered by high-resolution textures, volumetric atmospheric fog, ray-traced dynamic lighting, and realistic shadow effects.
- No global daytime lighting: the environment is dark, lit only by player flashlights, flickering emergency lights, and red alarm beacons.
- Extremely detailed indoor environments: abandoned underground medical complex, peeling wallpaper, cracked floor tiles, bloodstains, floating dust particles, and broken glass.

3. INTRO, GAME START @COMMENT_BODY@ STORY LORE:
- Game Intro: Starts with a cinematic cutscene. The player wakes up in a dark, locked security office. On a wooden desk sits a flickering lamp, a cassette recorder, and a blood-stained journal explaining the lore—an illegal genetic containment breach of a sound-sensitive host creature.
- Game Start: Players gather their starting items (a dying flashlight and a walkie-talkie) and must unlock the main security door to enter the facility.

4. OBJECTIVE @COMMENT_BODY@ GAME COMPLETION (WIN/LOSE CONDITIONS):
- Primary Objective: Navigate through 3 distinct sectors (Medical, Labs, Reactor) to collect 3 encrypted keycards, restore the main power generator, and activate the surface elevator.
- How the Game Ends (Victory): All surviving players must reach the surface elevator, call it down, defend the position for 60 seconds against the creature, and board the elevator to escape.
- Defeat Condition: If all players die or if the facility triggers its auto-detonation sequence before escaping, the game is lost.

5. SINGLEPLAYER MODE:
- Immersive, atmospheric solo experience with zero HUD on screen. 
- Health, stamina, and fear are displayed through in-game cues (heavy breathing, visible pulse, blurriness, blood splatters on screen).

6. MULTIPLAYER HUB @COMMENT_BODY@ MATCHMAKING:
Create a full-featured multiplayer system with three distinct options:
- A) Custom Private Lobby (Code System): The host creates a private lobby that generates a unique 4-character room code. Friends can enter this code in the menu to join the private session immediately.
- B) Quick Play (Public Matchmaking): One-click matchmaking that instantly pairs the player with random online players worldwide into an active 2-4 player lobby.
- C) Offline / Bot Match: Option to play multiplayer maps offline or fill empty slots with intelligent, cooperative AI bot teammates.

7. GAMEPLAY MECHANICS:
- 2 to 4 player co-op with proximity voice chat (creatures can hear players talking if they speak too loudly).
- Teamwork mechanics: sharing flashlight batteries, completing two-person puzzle interactions, and carrying/reviving downed teammates.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

input.prompt: Inspect repository structure and identify the existing app/game entrypoint, technologies, run/build scripts, and current state. Recommend exact files to modify to implement user's playable horror game request. Do not edit files.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e48f442d7ffegocx5ptpXssiEQ" state="completed">
## Repository findings

- **No existing app or game entrypoint is present.** There is no `index.html`, `src/` directory, `package.json`, or application JavaScript/TypeScript.
- **Technologies:** The repository contains no app framework or dependency manifest. The only evident runtime technology is Node.js, used by an external runtime wrapper; a simple browser game could be added without introducing a framework.
- **Run/capture wrappers:**
  - [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh) invokes `${RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/default-start.mjs`.
  - [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh) invokes `${RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/default-capture.mjs`.
  - Both require `RUNTIME_DIR`; neither defines app-specific build or development commands.
  - [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/startup.sh`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/startup.sh) currently contains only strict-shell settings.
- **Current state:** The tracked project files are the README and a GitHub Actions workflow. The working tree also has untracked harness/config files: `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`. I did not modify anything.

## Suggested files for the horror game

Since there is no app to extend, implement the game as a small browser app by creating:

1. `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` — page shell and game mount point.
2. `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js` — gameplay, input, game state, and rendering.
3. `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css` — game and responsive control styling.

Keep the existing start/capture wrappers unchanged initially. Add a `package.json` only if the chosen implementation requires dependencies or the external runtime needs explicit project scripts; the repository currently provides no evidence that one is required.
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable survival horror game titled “The Facility: Null” in this repository.

## Requirements
- Title screen credit: “Created by °-° KING LOOK.S”; German-default and English UI localization; English radio/dialogue.
- Dark, atmospheric underground facility with Medical, Labs, and Reactor sectors, flashlight, hazards, and a sound-sensitive creature.
- Collect three keycards, restore generator, reach elevator, survive a 60-second defense, and escape; all-death or detonation means defeat.
- Single-player with no persistent HUD; settings and multiplayer lobby options, including private codes, quick play, and offline bots.
- Co-op mechanics requested include proximity voice chat, sharing batteries, two-person puzzles, and carrying/reviving teammates.
- User requested a playable implementation without clarification and screenshots for checks: JPEG at most 1280px wide, inspect only latest.

## Decisions
- No existing app was found, so created a dependency-free browser game using HTML, CSS, and Canvas raycasting.
- Multiplayer matchmaking/lobbies are explicitly presented as locally simulated; online co-op needs a server.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a title/menu, German-English localization switch, settings panel, lobby UI, intro/logbook, controls, and responsive/mobile controls.
- Implemented a procedural first-person raycaster, multi-sector map, movement, flashlight/battery, sound-reactive creature, keycards, generator, elevator defense/escape, and offline follower bots.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Implementation is unverified in a browser; no screenshot/capture was performed.
- Review/fix gameplay progression, user-requested multiplayer/co-op mechanics, and polish as needed.

### Blocked
- Real online matchmaking, networked co-op, and proximity voice chat require backend/server support; current lobby is a local simulation.

## Next Move
1. Run the app using the available project runtime and inspect gameplay in a browser.
2. Fix any runtime/rendering or progression issues, especially interaction reachability and elevator victory flow.
3. Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot as requested.
4. Report implemented scope and clearly note multiplayer/network limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell, menu, settings, lobby, intro, HUD, journal, and controls.
- `style.css`: Menu/panel styling, atmospheric overlay, responsive layout, and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Localization, Canvas rendering, map, input, gameplay state, creature, objectives, bots, and progression.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; new `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js` were created.
- `game.js` passed syntax validation, but browser behavior has not been tested.
- Browser game uses procedural visuals and synthesized tones; no external game assets or professional voice acting are present.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
